page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7H12 processor, running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor exhibits average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6113.37 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7366.0. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 763.49, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested instances. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 742.7 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak at 29.99 GB/sec and 15.38 GB/sec respectively. Despite these memory bandwidth limitations, the instance maintains solid database and caching capabilities, achieving 14.27 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r6a.4xlarge provides a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive single-threaded CPU performance. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs reduces overhead for deployments focused purely on memory capacity. This hardware profile is well-suited for in-memory databases, caching layers such as Redis, enterprise applications, and general-purpose workloads requiring substantial RAM.
